summary: Barbers Point Light, Oahu: an 1888 coral-stone tower replaced by a 1933 concrete tower; keeper Manuel Ferreira's rescues, and the 1906 Sheridan stranding.

lens.where: Lantern room and fourth-order lens removed when the light was automated in 1964; on display at the Columbia River Maritime Museum, Astoria, Oregon (LighthouseFriends).

structures.note: Cylindrical reinforced-concrete tower, 72 feet, beside the old tower (Bulletin 1934).

corrections.why: The 1888 coral-stone tower was replaced by the present reinforced-concrete tower in 1933 (Bulletin 1934; LighthouseFriends). The record's 'built 1888, concrete' mixes the two towers.
The 1934 Bulletin gives the new focal plane as 86 feet (26.2 m). The Digital Archive record gives a 50-foot focal height for the station, which is not reconciled here.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two towers: the coral-stone tower of 1888 (42 ft, lit 29 March 1888) and the concrete tower of 1933 (72 ft, lit 29 December 1933). The 'different first years' note in the record comes from treating them as one.
The 'more than 3 m' difference is between the 1888 tower (42 ft, 12.8 m) and the 1933 tower (72 ft, 22 m), per the Bulletin and LighthouseFriends.

notes_for_editor: CHECKED 2026-10-22 (fact-check). (1) NRHP 100010117 (listed 2024 per the record) was not read: the NPGallery asset page returned no text, and the nomination was not located. The story does not state the listing date. (2) Focal height: the 1934 Bulletin says 86 ft (26.2 m); the record says 25.9 m; the Digital Archive gives a 50-ft focal height. Not reconciled; the story does not give a focal height. (3) Owner: LighthouseFriends says the Coast Guard owns the light (its page says 'Grounds open, tower closed'). The record has no agency. Other listings name a city parks department as operator of the adjoining park; not verified here. Confirm the current owner before publishing 'Today'. (4) The 1919 rescue of seven fishermen is from LighthouseFriends only. The Commissioner's aid tables (1915-1922 volume) name Ferreira in a column-run OCR table; the entry was not matched by position and is not cited. (5) The 1941 letter is quoted only as LighthouseFriends prints it (LighthouseFriends prints 'the Fort Kam. 55th C.A. boys'); the Honolulu papers for December 1941 were not searched for it. (6) Stranding time: the Hawaiian Star gives 1:48 a.m. The Pacific Commercial Advertiser's time is garbled in the OCR, so no PCA time is given. (7) Sweeney's dates conflict (Digital Archive 1941-1948; LighthouseFriends 1941-1942). The story gives his 1941 role only. (8) LighthouseFriends spells the point's namesake 'Baber' once; the story uses Barber, as the rest of the page does. The story no longer says the point is named for him; LighthouseFriends says only that it has been associated with him since the wreck. (9) 'James Conrad (1945-1947)' appears in a search-result lead only; not on the roster; not added. (10) Bulletin 1934 OCR has errors ('reinfcrced', '~alakaua'); the story spells the king's name Kalakaua, outside the quotation. (11) Robins' family details (a daughter's 1958 stay) are omitted under the living-persons rule. Robins' service ended in 1964; the story names him only in his public role. (12) Caroline Ferreira: LighthouseFriends does not say she was his wife, so the story gives her name and her role without a relationship. The influenza episode is LighthouseFriends only. (13) Honolulu newspapers for 1888 (the first keeper's appointment and the contractor) were not searched; those details come from LighthouseFriends. (14) The 1923 Bianca account: the Bulletin gives 14 January for the anchoring and 3 miles for the walk; LighthouseFriends says Ferreira 'ran over three miles' and a Navy tug towed her. The story uses the Bulletin's wording.
